title: Can’t Patch PHP2Shell Yet? Build a Stopgap with the Controls You Own
content_md: PHP2Shell comes with a clear instruction: update PHP. Fixed releases exist for supported branches, and Qualys customers can identify PHP installations using network scans, Cloud Agents, container assessments, and Deep Scan where supported, while assessing exposed web applications and APIs with Qualys TotalAppSec. Patching at this scale still takes time. In Qualys telemetry, only 199,000 of the 156 million PHP package installations with a known version had been patched during the first 12 hours after disclosure. Those first days are where mitigations and compensating controls earn their place. They reduce risk while updates roll out, and the right visibility shows which servers need attention first. Our PHP2Shell guide covers detection and fixed versions. Here is how to bridge the gap between disclosure and patch. Start with Qualys Mitigation Qualys provides a configuration-level mitigation for PHP2Shell based on PHP’s guidance and insights from the Qualys Threat Research Unit. It disables session upload progress and hardens related session-handling configuration on supported hosts. This reduces exposure to the confirmed session-lifecycle attack path without requiring application-code changes. It does not eliminate every exploitation path associated with the two CVEs. Applications that depend on upload-progress functionality should be tested after the change. Configuration-level, with restart verification .
